judge_output.rationale: Zackrisson et al. 2018 searched for optically subluminous stars, flagged by parallax distances shorter than their spectrophotometric distances, in RAVE DR5 × Gaia DR1, and checked infrared excess only for one follow-up star. The Hephaistos papers, Contardo et al. 2024 and the earlier WISE/IRAS searches test only the infrared-excess half, using WISE photometry. None of the listed abstracts reports a population-level test that requires the optical deficit to equal the integrated 1-5 um excess luminosity, nor a grey-versus-chromatic dimming test with Gaia XP and SPHEREx. The card is therefore a joint, energy-balance version of two halves that have each been tested separately with older or different data.

closest_prior.relation: Tested optical subluminosity (spectrophotometric distance exceeding parallax distance) in RAVE DR5 × Gaia DR1 and found no infrared excess in its follow-up star; it did not quantify a deficit-equals-excess balance and used neither XP spectra nor 1-5 um spectrophotometry.

Searched for infrared excess fitted with a photosphere-plus-blackbody model in about 5 million Gaia DR3/2MASS/WISE sources; it did not compare against an optical luminosity deficit, and its candidates were later attributed to background galaxies.
Data-driven search for W1/W2 excess in about 4.9 million FGK main-sequence stars, reporting fractional excess luminosities of 0.005-0.1, with no matched optical deficit test.
Points out that such structures could make stars appear anomalously faint in optical catalogues, which motivates a deficit-based search, but does not carry out one.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: No listed work measures, per star, both the isochrone-relative optical bolometric deficit and the integrated 1-5 um excess luminosity (Gaia XP + SPHEREx) for spectroscopic dwarfs and tests whether D equals E together with grey dimming.
